sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:239522
Court No. - 69
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 50927 of 2023

Applicant :- Rajkumar
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Sanjai Kumar Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J.
1. List revised.
2. Heard Sri Sanjai Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Triveni Saran, learned counsel for the State and perused the material on record.

3. This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant Rajkumar, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No.
0290 of 2022, under Sections 376, 504, 506 I.P.C., registered at Police Station Sevrahi, District Kushinagar.

Rajkumar vs State Of U.P. on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154394470/
1

4. Learned counsel for the State submits that he has received instructions for which time was granted to him vide order dated 29.11.2023.
5.

The FIR of the matter was lodged on 04.10.2022 by the victim herself against the applicant on the basis of an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. alleging therein that on 06.07.2022 at about 08:00 pm she was walking near the canal where the applicant finding her alone gagged her mouth and took her behind the field of banana and committed rape upon her and threatened her.
Her husband is a labour and works outside village.
She informed about the incident at the police station but no action was taken.

Then an application dated 30.07.2022 was moved under Section 156(3)
Cr.P.C.
6.
Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the victim on her own showing is a married woman.
She has disclosed her age as 23 years in application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.

It is argued that the FIR has been lodged with malafides just in order to falsely implicate and harass the applicant since the sister of the applicant has lodged an FIR as Case Crime No. 237 of 2021 under Section 376 IPC,
P.S. Sevrahi, District Kushinagar on 05.10.2021 against Amit Chaurasia, Harinath and Phoolkali in which Amit Chaurasia was assigned the role of committing rape upon her and he is the devar of the first informant of the case.
It is argued that thus the present FIR has been lodged since Amit Chaurasia was arrested and then he was granted bail and an effort settling the matter failed.
It is argued that the investigation concluded and charge sheet has been submitted against the applicant.
It is argued that the victim was produced before the doctor who refused her internal medical examination and such there is no corroboration of rape from medical evidence.
He further argued that the applicant has no criminal history as stated in para 22 of the affidavit and he is in jail since 15.10.2023.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for bail.
8. After having heard learned counsel for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the victim is a major married woman as stated in application moved under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.
The FIR has been lodged on the basis of an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.
The case is of false implication due to FIR lodged against the devar of the first informant by the sister of the applicant.

9. Looking to the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of evidence and also the absence of any convincing material to indicate the possibility of tampering with the evidence, this Court is of the view that the applicant may be enlarged on bail.

10. Let the applicant Rajkumar, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
Rajkumar vs State Of U.P. on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154394470/
2 ii) The applicant will abide the orders of court, will attend the court on every date and will not delay the disposal of trial in any manner whatsoever.
(iii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iv) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.

In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under section 174-A I.P.C.
(v) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law and the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A IPC.

(vi) The trial court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously after the release of the applicant.
11.

The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
12. The bail application is allowed.

Order Date :- 18.12.2023 M. ARIF (Samit Gopal, J.)
